bib.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; Appendix proof text (A.1 steps, A.5 lemma proofs) read for structure, volunteer name list and sample-output tables not recorded

question: Can a language model be fit directly to human preference data with a simple classification loss, optimizing the same KL-constrained reward objective as RLHF without a reward model or RL loop?
hypothesis: A change of variables from reward to optimal policy lets the Bradley-Terry preference loss be written over the policy directly, so DPO should match or beat PPO-based RLHF while being simpler and more stable.
contributions: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), a simple RL-free algorithm for training language models from preferences
Theory: the reparameterization r = beta log(pi/pi_ref) loses no generality over reward classes (Theorem 1) and the gradient weights examples by implicit-reward error
Experiments on sentiment, TL;DR summarization and Anthropic-HH dialogue up to 6B parameters, plus a human study validating GPT-4 as judge

method.summary: DPO minimizes -log sigma(beta log pi_theta(yw|x)/pi_ref(yw|x) - beta log pi_theta(yl|x)/pi_ref(yl|x)) over a fixed offline preference dataset, with pi_ref the SFT model. It is compared with PPO RLHF, Best-of-N, preferred-FT, unlikelihood and prompting on IMDb sentiment (GPT-2-large), TL;DR summarization (GPT-J 6B SFT) and Anthropic-HH dialogue (Pythia-2.8B), judged by GPT-4 win rate.

datasets.name: IMDb (controlled sentiment)
datasets.size: prompts are 2-8 token review prefixes; 4 completions sampled for 25000 prefixes, 6 preference pairs per prefix
datasets.split: SFT on train split subset for 1 epoch
datasets.source: IMDb [Maas et al.]; ground-truth reward siebert/sentiment-roberta-large-english
datasets.preprocessing: Preference pairs built with the sentiment classifier so p(positive|x,yw) > p(positive|x,yl)

datasets.name: Reddit TL;DR summarization + Stiennon et al. preferences
datasets.source: Reddit TL;DR [Voelske et al.] with human preferences from Stiennon et al.
datasets.preprocessing: Preferences were gathered on samples from a different, similarly-trained SFT model

datasets.name: Anthropic Helpful and Harmless (HH)
datasets.split: subset of test split with one human-assistant step used for eval
datasets.preprocessing: No SFT model available, so Pythia-2.8B is fine-tuned on preferred completions only

datasets.name: CNN/DailyMail
datasets.preprocessing: Same GPT-4 (C) prompt with 'forum post' replaced by 'news article'

other.use: sentiment policy and RLHF reward model init

models.name: Pythia-2.8B
models.init_from: Preferred-FT on chosen completions gives pi_ref

other.order: order of the two candidates randomised per evaluation

training.objective: L_DPO = -E[log sigma(beta log pi_theta(yw|x)/pi_ref(yw|x) - beta log pi_theta(yl|x)/pi_ref(yl|x))]; pi_ref = pi_SFT, or max-likelihood on preferred completions if SFT unavailable
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup from 0 to 1e-6, then constant (inferred: no decay stated)
training.steps: evaluated every 100 steps until convergence; dialogue curve runs to about 3300 steps (read from Fig 3)
training.regularisation: beta KL strength: 0.1 default, 0.5 for TL;DR
training.seeds: random seeds varied only for Preferred-FT in the sentiment sweep; otherwise not stated

other.ppo_batch_sentiment: 1024 samples per PPO step in own implementation
other.rlhf_reward_model: initialised from gpt2-large, 3 epochs, best validation-accuracy checkpoint
other.beta_tuning: authors say they did not meaningfully tune beta

inference.temperature: TL;DR: swept 0.0 to 1.0, DPO best at 0.25 in human study; dialogue: 0.7 and 1.0 shown in Fig 3
inference.samples: Best of N baseline with N up to 128 (dialogue) and 256 (TL;DR); other sample counts per prompt not stated
inference.prompting: GPT-J zero-shot on TL;DR; Pythia-2.8B 2-shot on dialogue

other.max_generation: samples in Tables 7 and 9 end with [maximum generation length reached]; limit not stated

metrics.name: Reward vs KL frontier
metrics.definition: Average true sentiment reward against average sequence-level KL(pi||pi_ref) (sum of per-timestep KLs) on test prompts

metrics.name: GPT-4 win rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of test prompts where GPT-4 prefers the method's output over the baseline (reference summary for TL;DR, chosen response for HH)

metrics.name: Human-GPT-4 agreement
metrics.definition: Raw agreement percentage per judgment, ties (about 1%) ignored

baselines: PPO (learned reward, own tuned implementation with reward normalisation)
PPO-GT (oracle reward; own and TRL versions)
Best of N (128 for HH, up to 256 for TL;DR)
eval.protocol: Sentiment: 22-run sweep, evaluated every 100 steps. Summarization and dialogue: GPT-4 win rate across temperatures; human study with 25 volunteer raters, 25 comparisons each (150 DPO-vs-PPO, 100 PPO-1-vs-PPO-0 with two humans each, 125 SFT with one human). No significance tests or multiple training seeds reported.

availability.data: public datasets; SFT checkpoint huggingface CarperAI/openai_summarize_tldr_sft

evidence.quote: For TL;DR summarization, we use β = 0.5, while rest of the parameters remain the same.

results.claim: DPO reaches about 61% GPT-4 win rate against reference summaries on TL;DR at temperature 0.0.
results.setup: TL;DR test split, GPT-J 6B SFT, GPT-4 (C) prompt, DPO beta 0.5
results.quote: We find that DPO has a win rate of approximately 61% at a
results.note: Read from Fig 2 right; stated as approximate

results.claim: PPO reaches 57% win rate at its best sampling temperature 0.0.
results.setup: TL;DR test split, same GPT-J SFT, PPO with learned reward
results.quote: exceeding the performance of PPO at 57% at its optimal sampling temperature of 0.0.

results.claim: In a head-to-head human evaluation DPO (temp 0.25) samples were preferred over PPO (temp 0) samples.
results.setup: TL;DR, DPO temp 0.25 vs PPO temp 0
results.quote: preferred 58% times over PPO samples at temperature 0.
results.table: Table 2, row Human win %, column DPO

results.claim: On the sentiment task DPO gives the most efficient reward-KL frontier, beating PPO even when PPO has ground-truth reward.
results.setup: IMDb, GPT-2-large, 22-run hyperparameter sweep, true reward from sentiment classifier
results.quote: This sweep includes 22 runs in total.
results.note: Frontier is a plot (Fig 2 left); no numeric value in text

results.claim: DPO out-of-distribution on CNN/DailyMail beats PPO: win rate vs ground-truth summaries at temp 0.
results.setup: Policies trained on Reddit TL;DR, evaluated on CNN/DailyMail test, GPT-4 (C) prompt
results.table: Table 1, row DPO column Temp 0 (0.36; Temp 0.25 0.31) vs row PPO (0.26; 0.23)

results.claim: GPT-4 (C) win rate for DPO vs greedy PPO is 54% against 58% for humans; GPT-4 agrees with humans about as often as humans agree with each other (DPO comparison: GPT-4(C)-human 67, human-human 65).
results.setup: TL;DR, DPO temp 0.25 vs PPO temp 0
results.table: Table 2, row GPT-4 (C) win %, column DPO (54); Human win % (58); GPT-4 (C)-H agree (67); H-H agree (65)

results.claim: On Anthropic-HH dialogue DPO is the only computationally efficient method that improves over the dataset's preferred completions; Best of N plateaus at roughly 64-128 samples.
results.setup: Pythia-2.8B, HH one-step test subset, GPT-4 win rate vs chosen
results.note: Win rates are shown only in Fig 3

results.claim: A public PPO-trained HH model gave no prompt or temperature better than base Pythia-2.8B.
results.note: Authors therefore treat Best of 128 as a rough proxy for PPO-level performance

results.claim: Unlikelihood training produces meaningless text on summarization and dialogue (repeated tokens), so it is only a sentiment baseline.
results.quote: unlikelihood fails to generate meaningful responses for more complex problems such as summarization and dialogue.

results.claim: A naive objective without the per-example weight degenerates the model; the gradient weights examples by how wrongly the implicit reward orders the pair.
results.quote: a naïve version of this method without the weighting coefficient can cause the language model to degenerate (Appendix Table 3)
results.note: Evidence is the unlikelihood samples, not a separate ablation

results.claim: DPO samples can be verbose and hallucinate; GPT-4 sometimes judges wrongly (7 plus 2 example).

limits: Models only up to 6B parameters; scaling to much larger models untested
Out-of-distribution generalisation evidence is initial (one CNN/DailyMail test)
Whether reward over-optimisation occurs under DPO is open; the slight decline in Fig 3 right may be an instance
GPT-4 win rates depend on the prompt (S prefers longer summaries than humans)
DPO beta barely tuned (authors say results may underestimate DPO)
No multiple seeds or significance tests; compute and hardware not stated
PPO baselines on TL;DR/HH rely on authors' tuning and a public checkpoint, so baseline strength is uncertain
Preference data assumed sampled from pi_SFT; otherwise pi_ref is approximated by max-likelihood on preferred completions

terms.definition: r_hat_theta(x,y) = beta log pi_theta(y|x)/pi_ref(y|x), the reward implicitly defined by the language model and reference model
Two reward functions are equivalent iff r(x,y) - r'(x,y) = f(x) for some function f
Sample N responses from the SFT (or Preferred-FT) model and return the highest-scoring under a learned reward function
A model fine-tuned with supervised learning on the chosen completion yw
